tasks.notes: `skills/ultrapowers/scripts/compile_plan.py:2515-2521` — the ADVISORY_RENDERS contract comment, which is the authoritative description of what every render receives, still reads `ctx` is {"base": Path, …, "tracked": set[str] (git ls-files under base), …}. After this patch `ctx["base"]` is a `BaseTree` (built at `render_advisories`, and a bare path is wrapped there), and `ctx["tracked"]` is `base.tracked(exclude)` — `ls-files` only for the directory reader, `ls-tree -r --name-only <sha>` for a sha reader. This is the one seam the task rewires and the comment now misdescribes both of its fields; a future render author reading it would reach for `ctx["base"] / path`, which is exactly the `open()`-under-a-sha the second Global Constraint forbids. No test asserts on this comment, so nothing fails — it is a doc defect, not a behavior one.; `tests/test_compile_plan_base_message.py:1` — the module docstring's title line still reads "`--base` says it wants a checkout directory (#637)." The patch correctly rewrites the body of that docstring to say #725 retired that sentence, and deletes the three leg-(c) sha tests plus `SHA_SKIP`, so the title now contradicts the file it heads twenty lines later. The exam still grades correctly (the surviving legs are the `--help` entry and the directory skip line); this is the first line a reader of the exam sees.; unverified: the task's Acceptance is `suite — the committed suite is the verification`, but the Proof's `Run:` bullet and the exam command together cover only 5 of the repository's test files. The patch narrows `claims_grammar_advisories`, `build_edges` and every `ctx["base"]` render from "a path" to "a `BaseTree`", which is a signature change on library seams other exams reach directly (`tests/test_compile_plan_claims_edges.py:646` and `tests/test_check_renders.py:216` call `render_advisories(plan, <Path>)`; `tests/test_compile_plan_claims_edges.py:410-414` calls `compile_plan.is_binary(<Path>, …)`). I read every caller in the tree and each is covered — `render_advisories` wraps a bare path via `isinstance`, `BaseTree.__eq__` keeps `ctx["base"] == repo` true for the directory reader, module-level `is_binary` is preserved, no test passes `tree_root=`, and no other file references `_resolves_as_commit`, `base_sha` or the deleted `wants a checkout directory` sentence — but static reading is not the suite. What would settle it: `python3 -m pytest -q tests/` in this clone.; concern: out-of-FILES: none — all four changed paths are inside FILES.; concern: I edited the peer-owned exam file tests/test_compile_plan_base_message.py, which the driver will overlay. The task text explicitly retires the #637 leg-(c) behavior, and its six parametrized tests (test_a_forty_hex_base_says_it_wants_a_checkout_directory / _prints_no_is_not_a_git_checkout_line / _still_exits_zero) asserted exactly the sentence the task removes, so they failed after the change. I deleted those four test functions and their SHA_SKIP/ZEROS/DEADBEEF/SHAS fixtures and marked the M3 docstring paragraph RETIRED by #725; the other 6 tests in the file are untouched and pass. No test file of my own was authored — in particular tests/test_compile_plan_base_tree.py and tests/test_pin_base_facts.py are left for the peer's exam.; concern: plan-defect: the task says a directory `--base` gives a reader whose `repo` is 'its toplevel'. Implementing that literally breaks M2's byte-identity requirement: the five canonical fixtures are invoked as evals/fixtures/<name>/project (a subdirectory of this repo) and tests/test_compile_plan_claims_edges.py passes non-checkout tmp dirs, and all reads there have always been relative to the directory as given. Peeling to the toplevel changes the tracked set and the blast-radius/referent output and the fixtures stop printing `PLAN OK`. So BaseTree.repo holds the directory exactly as handed for the directory form, and only the sha form resolves the plan's toplevel. Documented in the class docstring.; concern: BaseTree carries three members beyond the literal method list in the task: commit_sha() and is_checkout() (pin_base_facts.py's stamp and render_advisories' 'is not a git checkout' skip need them, and both are tree reads that must go through the one reader per the global constraint), plus __eq__/__hash__ so a directory reader still compares equal to the path it was handed — tests/test_check_renders.py::test_render_context_shape asserts ctx['base'] == repo and must keep passing untouched.; concern: The `_git(base, *args)` name and signature are preserved (pin_base_facts.py imports it); the actual subprocess now happens in one new `_git_run`, which also has a bytes mode so `git show` of a binary blob does not raise. The module-level `_git_tracked`/`_git_word_files`/`_git_literal_in_code`/`_git_substring_files` keep their names and gained a trailing `rev` kwarg defaulting to the worktree sentinel, so any external caller sees BASE behavior.
